Symfony releases on a fixed, predictable schedule: a patch update roughly every month (bug fixes only), a minor version every six months in May and November (new features, no breaking changes), and a new major version every two years, always in November of odd years.
...
The major and LTS releases in each two-year cycle aren't the same thing, and they don't ship on their own separate schedules either, Symfony develops them together and releases them on the same day.
The final minor of the outgoing branch (for example, 6.4) becomes that branch's LTS release, while the new major (7.0) ships simultaneously with the same features but with deprecated code removed.
...
Each version has a stated minimum PHP requirement, but while that Symfony version is still maintained, it supports every PHP release that comes out afterward too, there's no upper cap.
